newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil bolsas see $3.5 bln foreign inflow in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Brazil bolsas see $3.5 bln foreign inflow in 1996.

text.p: Net foreign capital inflows to Brazilian bourses under Annex Four rules totalled $560.7 million in December, taking the total amount of foreign investment to $3.593 billion for the whole year of 1996, Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) said.
In 1995, net foreign inflows were only $528.2 million.
The Annex Four regulates investment in Brazilian shares, debentures and privatization bonds.
In a statement the CVM said December capital inflows amounted to $2.461 billion, against total outflows of $1.9 billion for the month.
Foreign investment portfolios totalled $27.9 billion in December 1996, the statement said.
Shares accounted for 91.96 percent of the foreign investment portfolios, followed by debentures with 4.73 percent and privatization bonds with 2.79 percent, it added.
